A point-of-care (POC) HIV1/2 testing using sputum is a useful strategy for conducting HIV surveillance, particularly in areas with low HIV endemicity. This testing method can help identify individuals who may be co-infected with tuberculosis (TB) and HIV. Since there is no investment on infrastructure, paramedical health professionals, especially in rural or peripheral areas, may be able to perform the test.

However, it's essential to note that solid culture for TB remains a crucial diagnostic tool for determining the true nature of pulmonary TB. Using POC tests should not replace clinical suspicion and diagnostic judgment. Additionally, more research is needed to optimize the implementation of POC testing in resource-limited settings, including scaling up infrastructure and ensuring adequate training for healthcare workers.
